OCR/import issues are directly linked to poorer onboarding performance and can degrade the quality of answers delivered by the support assistant. Scanned, image-only PDFs require OCR before KnowledgeHub can extract a usable text layer; without OCR, citation accuracy drops and tenants fail the go-live quality threshold (85% citation correctness, or 90% for Enterprise where applicable) [NL-015#NL-015-S04][NL-005#NL-005-S11][NL-031#NL-031-S04]. OCR processing is a distinct onboarding-delay category, accounting for 25% of delay incidents [NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-031#NL-031-S04]. For example, Northstar Financial needed external OCR preprocessing of scanned credit policy PDFs, delaying pilot kickoff by three weeks [NL-010#NL-010-S06], and BrightPath Healthcare had the longest onboarding duration at 9.5 weeks due to OCR/scanned-PDF compliance issues [NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-031#NL-031-S04]. Without OCR, ingestion can fail or yield incomplete text extraction, leaving TutorChat unable to answer basic queries or producing low-quality/missing answers [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. Large scanned-batch imports can also clog the ingestion queue and block normal uploads, requiring split-queue architecture and page caps to protect system performance [NL-021#NL-021-S06]. Onboarding blockers, including OCR/import issues, are reviewed against onboarding metrics and support ticket patterns [NL-031#NL-031-S04], though no quantitative evidence in the context directly ties OCR issues to support ticket volume.
